discussion.body:
Apex Legends maps use a `"*coll0" "<base64>"` form for triggers
Seems line an evolution of Titanfall 2's plaintext brushes & planes.

For decompiling & compiling maps we need to understand & re-create these structures.

## Structure sizes
```python
>>> {len(e["*coll0"]) for e in b.external.ENTITIES.search(classname="envmap_volume")}
{160}
>>> {len(e["*coll1"]) for e in b.external.ENTITIES.search(classname="envmap_volume")}
{160}
>>> {len(e["*coll2"]) for e in b.external.ENTITIES.search(classname="envmap_volume")}
{108}
```
### As bytes
```python
>>> len(base64.b64decode(b.external.ENTITIES[5]["*coll0"]))
120
>>> len(base64.b64decode(b.external.ENTITIES[5]["*coll1"]))
120
>>> len(base64.b64decode(b.external.ENTITIES[5]["*coll2"]))
80
```

`envmap_volume` appears to be a cuboid brush marking a space for parallax mapping cubemaps.
The Season 15 Lobby's only `coll*` ents are these, but other unrendered trigger volume types use `coll*`

None of the `envmap_volume` origins seem to align with their target cubemaps, or the center of their bounds:

```python
>>> {print(c) for c in b.external.CUBEMAPS}
```

According to @r-ex this is similar to `rmdl` collision
Though their 010 `.bt` crashed, might be some issues with indexing

Could we create a trigger w/ vscript and dump the `*coll` keyvalues?
Would make for a useful reference

Some entities have more than 3 `*coll` entries, the terminating entry can be variable length
e.g. `"model" "*179"` in `season14/9aug22/maps/mp_rr_aqueduct` goes up to `*coll32`

all `*coll` probably get combined into one bytestream to make a big variable-length struct

`*coll0` is always `160` chars long, the max for any `*coll` value
probably something to do with string parsing speed / interruptibilty

> all `*coll` probably get combined into one bytestream to make a big variable-length struct
rexx found the code for parsing `*coll` & this is indeed the case

`*coll` is apparently the same as physics structures in `.rmdl`

This means there's `BVHNode` & `BVHLeafData`
